p:cNvPr.descr: A ring-like structure representing transmembrane electrical potential; the hydrophobic and hydrophilic ends of the membrane are both visible. In part a, the electrogenic Na+ K+ ATPase establishes the membrane potential; in part b, ions tend to move down their electrochemical gradient across the polarized membrane. The ring-like structure represents the plasma membrane, with hydrophobic yellow tails and hydrophilic blue heads. The outer ring is surrounded by plus signs while the inner ring is surrounded by minus signs. At the top of the structure is a pink vertical rectangle, labeled Na+ K+ ATPase. Two curved arrows, one facing upward and the other, downward, pass through it – the arrow pointing upward on the outside points to 3 NA+, represented by small red spheres; the arrow pointing inward points to 2 K+, represented by small blue spheres. On the inside of the ring, NA+ K+ ATPase is connected to three structures, one purple, one yellow, and one green. A curved arrow also points from ATP (orange oval) to ADP (gray oval) [plus] Pi. Directly opposite on the bottom of the ring, there are four skinnier pink rectangles, labeled, from left to right, Low, Low, High, and Low. The first two pink compartments have blue arrows pointing upward, and the last two have arrows pointing downward. Below the first arrow on the outside, is a Na+ (arrow points away from it) and the text, “High,” underneath it. The second arrow points away from Ca2+, and has the text, “High” beneath it. The third arrow points toward K+ below it and the text, “Low” is written beneath it. The fourth arrow points to Cl- and has the text, “High” beneath it. The top part of the diagram is labeled a, and reads “The electrogenic Na+ K+ ATPase establishes the membrane potential.” Part b, labeled on the bottom, reads, “Ions tend to move down their electrochemical gradient across the polarized membrane.”
